## Oderberg transport fragment and a troop-situation query

**Sources on this page:** p211 A2, p211 B upper.

<a id="edition-cases-military-prague-route-and-situation-oderberg-transport-fragment-and-a-troop-situation-query"></a>



**Two additional physical records from the upper part of Childs p211 have source-reviewed readings.** The 176-coordinate second part is readable without repairs. A separate 68-coordinate query asks about the situation and the troops' behavior, with three word repairs. The lower three-part key-schedule message on the same page is [already cataloged separately](#edition-cases-radio-p211-key-schedule).

Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The unchanged published Nov19–21 key retains the credit of George Lasry and the research of Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker. The earlier OCR screen already recovered the complete second-part body; this edition supplies manual source review and exact accounting, without a first-decipherment claim.

| Record | Literal source coordinates | Raw fixed labels | Source edits | Geometry |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| p211 A2, upper section | 176 | 88/88 | None | Native frame |
| p211 B, upper section | 68 | 34/34 | 3 coordinate substitutions | Native frame |

Both lengths agree with the printed RICHI labels. No coordinate is inserted, deleted, excluded or reordered. “Fixed” means fixed under the published square; it does not independently authenticate numeral or reference labels.

<a id="edition-cases-military-prague-route-and-situation-a2-the-first-part-is-explicitly-missing"></a>

### A2: the first part is explicitly missing

The upper section is headed **INTERCEPTED BY BRITISH STATIONS**, **20 November 1918**. The A header gives unknown sender and receiver, reception on **21 November**, and the message field **2317 (11/20)**. Immediately above the ciphertext it says **“1st TL missing”**, followed by **2 TL, RICHI-176**.

The literal 88-label reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ODERBERGKEINESCHWIERIGKEITENINDENWEGLEGENWIRDXXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXXOHLXRMJAJJ9JJOPXGEH
```

</details>

The surviving clause ends with “will place no difficulties in the way,” followed by a request to acknowledge receipt. Its beginning names Oderberg. The missing first part contains the subject and preceding context, so this fragment alone does not identify who made the undertaking, what complete route was involved, or a final permission decision. The closing `OHL X RMJAJJ9JJ OP X GEH` remains exactly as deciphered; no J or 9 is normalized into a different reference format.

The final glyph in printed group 26 is D, as confirmed by the enlarged source crop. It is retained as an observed coordinate, not treated as an erasure or a conjectural fill.

<a id="edition-cases-military-prague-route-and-situation-possible-relationship-to-the-prague-fragment-on-p209"></a>

#### Possible relationship to the Prague fragment on p209

The [p209 A1 edition](209.md#edition-cases-military-transport-and-disarmament-orders) is explicitly part 1 of a two-part message. Its final words are `AUFSTRECKETESCHEN`. This p211 part begins `ODERBERGKEINESCHWIERIGKEITENINDENWEGLEGENWIRD`. The two fragments therefore make a coherent **Teschen–Oderberg** route-name continuation, and both use the published Nov19–21 key.

That textual fit is useful, but the headers do not establish that these are the two parts of the same telegram:

| Evidence | p209 A1 | p211 A2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Printed part | 1 of 2 | 2; first part explicitly missing |
| Sender/receiver | `ZO'N v LP` | Not recorded |
| Message field | `22.35 (19/11)` | `2317 (11/20)` |
| Reception date | 19 November | 21 November |

The relationship is therefore recorded as a **possible companion**, with the date and time mismatch retained. Neither package's frozen source is changed, and no complete combined message or definitive transport permission is asserted.

<a id="edition-cases-military-prague-route-and-situation-b-upper-section-situation-and-conduct-of-troops"></a>

### B, upper section: situation and conduct of troops

This is the short B immediately below the transport fragment, before the horizontal division and the separate 19 November key-schedule message. Its header reads `ZON v LP (04.49 p.m., November 20th)`, `1645 (11/20)`, `RICHI-68`.

The unchanged source yields:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WIELAGEDORTXWIRVERHALTANDERTRUPPAN
```

</details>

The editorial proposal is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
WIELAGEDORTXWIEVERHALTENDERTRUPPEN
```

</details>

With spacing and punctuation: **“Wie Lage dort? Wie Verhalten der Truppen?”** It asks about the situation there and the behavior of the troops. The context does not identify which troops or location.

The proposal costs exactly three observed-coordinate substitutions, using zero-based indices:

| Source index | Printed → proposed | Affected word |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 22 | V → F | `VERHALTAN` → `VERHALTEN` |
| 23 | V → F | `TRUPPAN` → `TRUPPEN` |
| 34 | G → D | `WIR` → `WIE` |

All three are local word repairs under the unchanged square. There are no source-mask fills or additional plaintext characters.

<a id="edition-cases-military-prague-route-and-situation-evidence-and-reproduction"></a>

### Evidence and reproduction

The [inputs](../../experiments/prague_route_and_situation/inputs.json) preserve both diplomatic transcriptions, all header fields, the published key provenance and four source crops. The [certificates](../../experiments/prague_route_and_situation/certificates.json) record every plaintext pair's source coordinates and all three repairs. The [earlier candidate snapshot](../../experiments/prague_route_and_situation/prior_evidence.json) preserves the prior complete A2 reading.

```bash
python experiments/prague_route_and_situation/verify.py --verify
python experiments/prague_route_and_situation/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

The default verifier uses only the Python standard library. Optional PyMuPDF verification checks the exact source PDF hash and crop pixels. The [experiment README](../../experiments/prague_route_and_situation/README.md) states the finite scope and the unresolved relationship between the two transport fragments.

## p211, lower B — an explicit November/December key schedule

**Sources on this page:** p211 B lower1, p211 B lower2, p211 B lower3.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p211-key-schedule-p211-lower-b--an-explicit-novemberdecember-key-schedule"></a>



**Status:** Three source-checked parts form a readable key-handling
instruction. The unchanged published `Nov4-6` key fixes **265 of 266 raw
plaintext positions** from **532 printed coordinate slots**. **Source
assembly and edition:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. Period-key recovery
retains the attribution in [data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json); no first
historical decipherment priority is claimed.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p211-key-schedule-reading"></a>

### Reading

**Readable German:**

> November-Ringbahnschluessel nicht vernichten. Nachr.-Chef X4, B848727.
> Dezember-Ringbahnschluessel tritt vorlaeufig nicht in Kraft. Dafuer
> Schluessel erster Dezember wie zehnter November usw. bis
> einundzwanzigster Dezember wie dreissigster November.
> Empfangsbestaetigung. Nachr.-Chef Z4, B47857.

**Meaning:** Do not destroy the November Ringbahn key. The December Ringbahn
key will not yet take effect. Instead, use the 10 November key for 1 December,
continuing through the 30 November key for 21 December, and acknowledge
receipt.

The schedule itself is directly decoded in part 2 and the beginning of part
3. Three source-coordinate substitutions restore spelling in part 1; one
invalid source glyph is filled in `DREISSIGSTER` in part 3. Word spacing,
punctuation, abbreviation breaks and the omission of doubled separator `X`
characters in the reading above are editorial. The first reference
`B848727` and the difference between `NACHRCHEFX4` and `NACHRCHEFZ4` remain
literal; they are not regularized to each other.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p211-key-schedule-what-this-establishes"></a>

### The instructed December key schedule

This message records an explicit reuse instruction:

| Intended December date | November key named by the instruction |
| --- | --- |
| 1 December | 10 November |
| Continuing dates (`USW`) | Corresponding continuation of the November sequence |
| 21 December | 30 November |

The first and last mappings are explicit; the intermediate daily mapping is
the ordinary interpretation of `USW` (“and so on”). This is evidence of what
was instructed. It is not independent proof that every station followed the
instruction or that a particular December intercept uses a specified key.

The earlier [p189 C instruction](189.md#edition-cases-context-p189-c), including the raw word
`IRRTUM`, remains a separate source. The new schedule does not establish what
the earlier “error” meant. It does provide a concrete reason to examine
November/December key reuse without changing the wording of either message.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p211-key-schedule-source-identity-and-dates"></a>

### Source identity and dates

The [source crop](../../experiments/open_targets_continuation/sources/childs_p211_selected.png)
is printed p211 / PDF page 214. That page contains two different `B` labels under
different headings. This case concerns the **lower B**, following a new
**19 November 1918** heading:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
POT v NKJ (09.48 a.m., November 22d)
FUER POT COS VON LP SS DD 2230 3 TLE
1 TL: RICHI-214
2 TL: RICHI-184
3 TL: RICHI-134
```

</details>

The page heading, the 22 November receipt and the undated `2230` internal
time are all preserved. The later receipt does not justify relabelling the
published `Nov4-6` key, which directly decodes all three parts. These records
are locally named `p211_B_lower1`, `p211_B_lower2` and `p211_B_lower3` to avoid
confusing them with the upper B.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p211-key-schedule-literal-plaintext-and-exact-repair-costs"></a>

### Literal plaintext and exact repair costs

Part 1, 214 slots / 107 fixed plaintext positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
NOVEMBERXGINGBAHNSC7LUESSELNICHTVERNICHTENXNACHRCHEFX4XB848727XXDEZRMBERXRINGBAHNSCHLUESSELTRITTVORLAEUFIGX
```

</details>

The proposed `GINGBAHN→RINGBAHN`, `SC7LUESSEL→SCHLUESSEL` and
`DEZRMBER→DEZEMBER` each cost one known-coordinate substitution:
source indices **89: V→A**, **128: D→G** and **209: V→F**.
All other 211 coordinates stay unchanged.

Part 2, 184 slots / 92 fixed positions, needs no repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
NICHTINKRAFTXDAFUERSCHLUESSELERSTERDEZEMBERWIEZEHNTERNOVEMBERUSWBISEINUNDZWANZIGSTERDEZEMBER
```

</details>

Part 3, 134 slots / 66 of 67 fixed positions:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
WIEDREISSI?STERNOVEMBERXXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXXNACHRCHEFZ4XBX47857X
```

</details>

The printed `R` in `FRXXX` is outside the coordinate alphabet. Filling that
one slot, source index **16**, with `V` supplies the `G` in `DREISSIGSTER` and
preserves every one of the 133 valid coordinates. The three reconstructed
parts then re-encrypt exactly to the explicitly stated repaired witnesses.

The [p145 three-part witness](145.md#edition-cases-radio-nov6-ringbahn-key-witnesses) now supplies
independent raw support for all four proposed p211 word repairs:
`RINGBAHN`, `SCHLUESSEL`, `DEZEMBER` and the `G` in `DREISSIGSTER`.
Conversely, p211's unedited second part supports p145's declared one-slot
restoration and three substitutions; the resulting ciphertexts match
exactly. The copies retain their differing headings, reception dates and
literal reference fields. The additional witness strengthens the
transmitted wording, without establishing compliance with the key schedule.
